'''Alex Fudge''' (born May 6, 2003) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Ottawa BlackJacks]] of the [[Canadian Elite Basketball League]] (CEBL). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[LSU Tigers basketball|LSU Tigers]] and [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Florida Gators]]. 

==High school career==
Fudge played high school basketball at Robert E. Lee Senior High School (now named [[Riverside High School (Florida)|Riverside High School]]) in [[Jacksonville, Florida]].

===Recruiting===
Coming out of high school, Fudge was a highly ranked recruit in the Class of 2020. He was ranked as a 4-star recruit by both [[ESPN]] and [[247Sports]] recruiting services.<ref>{{cite web|title=Alex Fudge - ESPN recruiting|url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/242638/alex-fudge|website=ESPN.com|access-date=July 31, 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Alex Fudge - 247Sports recruiting|url=https://247sports.com/player/alex-fudge-46086502/high-school-239603/|website=247Sports.com|access-date=July 31, 2023}}</ref>

Fudge was heavily pursued by several universities and received 26 college offers according to 247Sports, alongside one Irish basketball team, the Sligo Allstars. From his 27 offers, Fudge narrowed his list down to 10 finalists, which included Alabama, Arkansas, Florida, Georgia, Georgia Tech, LSU, South Carolina, Texas, Texas A&M and UCF. Fudge ultimately committed to play basketball at LSU.<ref>{{cite web|first=Clayton|last=Freeman|title=Lee forward Alex Fudge commits to LSU|url=https://www.jacksonville.com/story/sports/high-school/basketball/2020/10/10/2021-forward-alex-fudge-lee-commits-lsu-basketball/5952602002/#|website=Jacksonville.com|date=October 10, 2010|access-date=July 31, 2023}}</ref>

==College career==
===LSU (2021–22)===
Fudge played one season for the LSU Tigers in 2021–22, averaging 3.3 points per game and appearing in 29 games as a freshman. Fudge appeared in the [[2022 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2022 NCAA tournament]] in the Tigers first round tourney loss to Iowa State. At LSU, Fudge played alongside future NBA players [[Tari Eason]] and [[Darius Days]]. During the season Fudge stubbed his toe playing shuffleboard and missed 1 match.

===Florida (2022–23)===
After one season at LSU, Fudge transferred to Florida for his sophomore season. At Florida, Fudge averaged 5.8 points and 4.5 rebounds per game and appeared in 32 games for the Gators.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Rudner |first1=Jacob |title=Florida forward Alex Fudge to declare for NBA Draft |url=https://247sports.com/college/florida/article/florida-basketball-roster-alex-fudge-nba-draft-todd-golden-gators-208314599/ |access-date=July 8, 2024 |work=247 Sports |date=April 13, 2023}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Los Angeles / South Bay Lakers (2023–2024)===
After going undrafted in the [[2023 NBA draft]], Fudge joined the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] for the [[2023 NBA Summer League]], averaging 3.0 points per game<ref>{{cite web|title=Lakers' Alex Fudge: Upgraded to two-way deal|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/lakers-alex-fudge-upgraded-to-two-way-deal/amp/|website=CBSSports.com|date=July 27, 2023|access-date=July 31, 2023}}</ref> and on July 26, 2023, he signed a [[two-way contract]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Los Angeles Lakers Sign Alex Fudge to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/news/los-angeles-lakers-sign-alex-fudge-to-two-way-contract-072623|website=NBA.com|date=July 27, 2023|access-date=July 31, 2023}}</ref> Fudge was honored as a part of the Lakers team that won the inaugural [[2023 NBA In-Season Tournament]] game. On January 6, 2024, he was waived by the Lakers along with [[D'Moi Hodge]]<ref>{{cite web|title=Lakers Waive Alex Fudge and D'Moi Hodge|url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/news/lakers-waive-alex-fudge-and-dmoi-hodge-010624|website=NBA.com|date=January 6, 2024|access-date=January 7, 2024}}</ref> and four days later, he joined the [[South Bay Lakers]].<ref>{{cite web|title=2023-2024 South Bay Lakers Transaction History|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/dleague/teams/South-Bay-Lakers/12/Transaction_History/2024|website=RealGM.com|access-date=January 10, 2024}}</ref>

===Dallas Mavericks / Texas Legends (2024)===
On March 4, 2024, Fudge signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Dallas Mavericks]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Eddie|last=Sefko|title=MAVERICKS SIGN FORMER LAKERS’ FORWARD TO TWO-WAY DEAL|url=https://www.mavs.com/mavs-sign-fudge/|website=Mavs.com|date=March 4, 2024|access-date=March 4, 2024}}</ref> Fudge reached the [[2024 NBA Finals|NBA Finals]] where the Mavericks lost to the [[Boston Celtics]] in 5 games. On August 27, he was waived by the Mavericks.<ref>{{cite web|title=MAVERICKS SIGN KESSLER EDWARDS TO TWO-WAY CONTRACT|url=https://texas.gleague.nba.com/news/mavericks-sign-kessler-edwards-to-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=August 27, 2024|access-date=August 27, 2024}}</ref>

===Return to South Bay (2024–2025)===
On September 5, 2024, Fudge signed with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]],<ref>{{cite web|title=Los Angeles Lakers Sign Alex Fudge|url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/news/los-angeles-lakers-sign-alex-fudge-090524|website=NBA.com|date=September 5, 2024|access-date=September 6, 2024}}</ref> but was waived the next day.<ref>{{cite tweet|author=Los Angeles Lakers|title=OFFICIAL: The Los Angeles Lakers have requested waivers on forward Alex Fudge.|number=1832150782168461802|user=Lakers|date=September 5, 2024|access-date=September 6, 2024}}</ref> On October 26, 2024, he rejoined the [[South Bay Lakers]].<ref>{{cite web|title=South Bay Lakers Finalize Training Camp Roster and Schedule|url=https://southbay.gleague.nba.com/news/south-bay-lakers-finalize-training-camp-roster-and-schedule|website=NBA.com|date=October 25, 2024|access-date=October 26, 2024}}</ref>

=== Sioux Falls Skyforce (2025–2026) ===
On September 16, 2025, Fudge was traded to the [[Sioux Falls Skyforce]] in a three-team trade involving the [[College Park Skyhawks]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Skyforce Acquires Alex Fudge |url=https://siouxfalls.gleague.nba.com/news/skyforce-acquires-alex-fudge |access-date=2026-05-27 |website=Sioux Falls Skyforce |language=en}}</ref>

=== Ottawa BlackJacks (2026–present) ===
On April 2, 2026, Fudge signed with the [[Ottawa BlackJacks]] of the [[Canadian Elite Basketball League]] (CEBL).<ref>{{Cite web |date=April 2, 2026 |title=OTTAWA BLACKJACKS SIGN FORWARD ALEX FUDGE |url=https://www.theblackjacks.ca/ottawa-blackjacks-sign-forward-alex-fudge}}</ref>

== National team career ==

===FIBA 3x3 U23 World Cup===
Fudge represented the US in the 2024 [[FIBA 3x3 U23 World Cup]]. This event marked Fudge's first time competing for USA Basketball.<ref>{{cite web |title=Alex Fudge to Represent USA in 3x3 U23 World Cup |url=https://floridagators.com/news/2024/9/10/mens-basketball-alex-fudge-to-represent-usa-in-3x3-u23-world-cup.aspx |website=Florida Gators |access-date=16 September 2024 |language=en}}</ref>
